p: beam: Or a piece of wood fit to build with.
swim: God wrought this miraculously to confirm the authority of Elisha, to whom he had given such abundance of his Spirit.
such and such a place shall: Meaning, that he would lie in ambush and take the Israelites unawares.
saved himself there: The wicked conspire nothing so craftily, but God can reveal it to his servants, and cause their counsel to be disclosed.
bedchamber: There is nothing so secret that you can go about, but he knows it, and reveals it to his king.
great host: Though it was nothing in man's judgment to have taken Elisha, yet the wicked doubt, and think they are never able to prepare enough power, though it be but against one or a few.
Fear not: For he was assured of God's help, and that millions of angels camped about the godly to deliver them.
that he may see: That he may behold how you have prepared an army to rescue us.
they came down to him: Meaning the Syrians his enemies, who came down thinking themselves sure of him.
them to Samaria: Thus he did being led by the Spirit of God, and not because he sought his own revenge, but only to set forth the glory of God.
My father: The wicked use reverent and grave words toward the servants of God, when they think to have any blessing from them, though in their heart they cannot abide them.

more into the land of Israel: For this gentle intreaty and the miracle wrought by the prophet, did more for peace than if they had been overcome in battle for they did not return at that time to fight against Israel, or in that king's days.
dung for five pieces of silver: The Hebrews write, that they burned it in the seige for lack of wood.
barnfloor: Meaning, any kind of food as corn and wine.
upon his flesh: Thus hypocrites when they feel God's judgments think to please him with outward ceremonies whom in prosperity they will not know.
murderer hath sent to take away: Meaning, Jehoram Ahab's son, who killed the prophets and caused Naboth to be stoned.
should I wait for the LORD: So the wicked fall into a rage and desperation, if they do not find a quick remedy for their afflictions.
